figures.title: f splits columns, g splits rows, one all-reduce closes the block
figures.caption: A tensor-parallel linear layer in two steps. f splits W by columns, so rank i computes y_i = xW_i with shape B×(K/N) and no collective. g splits V by rows, so each rank produces a partial sum z_i of shape B×M and an all-reduce sums them. The count is fixed at two collectives per block, 64 per forward for a 32-block model; the volume per collective is 2(N−1)/N × B×H per rank, which is B×H at N = 2 and 1.75 B×H at N = 8.
figures.alt: Three lanes across five steps. Rank 0 and rank 1 both start from the same x of shape B by H. In the f step each multiplies x by its own column slice of W, giving y-zero and y-one of shape B by K over N. In the g step each multiplies its y by its row slice of V, giving partial sums z-zero and z-one of shape B by M. The all-reduce step sums the partials on rank 0 while rank 1 waits; the link lane carries 2 times N minus 1 over N times B by H elements per rank. The next block repeats the pair.

data.note: At N = 2 the ring sends B×H elements per rank per collective; at N = 8 it sends 1.75 B×H. The pair decodes at 59.1 tok/s, so one forward pass takes 1000/59.1 = 16.9 ms; over 32 blocks and two collectives that is 64 collectives and a budget of 16.9/64 = 0.264 ms, or 264 µs, per collective. Above that round trip the schedule cannot hit 59.1 tok/s.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to follow the split through one block.

steps.label: x is replicated on both ranks: B×H.
f: each rank multiplies x by its column slice W_i; no collective.
g: each rank multiplies its y_i by its row slice V_i.
all-reduce sums the partials; rank 1 waits for the round trip.
The next block repeats the pair; 64 collectives per forward.

figures.title: Tensor parallelism pays per collective; pipeline pays per bubble
figures.caption: Tensor parallelism splits each layer's matrices and needs an all-reduce after every g: two collectives per block, 64 per forward for 32 blocks, which leaves 264 µs of the 16.9 ms forward pass per collective. Pipeline parallelism splits layers across ranks and needs a point-to-point send per micro-batch boundary; with P stages and M micro-batches the idle fraction is (P−1)/(M+P−1), 3/11 = 27.3% at P = 4, M = 8 and 3/19 = 15.8% at M = 16.
figures.alt: Two panels. The tensor-parallel panel lists: f computes y-i equals x W-i with W-i of shape H by K over N; g computes partial sums; an all-reduce follows each g; two collectives per block and 64 per 32-block forward; the per-collective budget is 264 microseconds; the ring moves 2 times N minus 1 over N times B by H. The pipeline panel lists: each rank holds whole layers; one send per micro-batch boundary; M times P minus 1 sends per direction; the bubble is P minus 1 over M plus P minus 1; 27.3 percent idle at four stages and eight micro-batches, 15.8 percent at sixteen.

panels.title: Pipeline parallel: per-bubble idle
panels.note: Doubling M cuts the bubble from 27% to 16%, a factor of about 1.7, not half. With P = 2 and L = 32, tensor parallelism issues 64 collective operations for every pipeline send.

data.note: The 264 µs cutoff is specific to this model, batch and collective size, not a general link threshold. The measured pair stall is 120,000 ms cumulative against 98 × 8.38 = 821 s of decode, about 15%; halving compute but doubling stall pays only while stall is below half the compute time.
